title: Afterimage in Brass
intent: A self-contained late-night noir jazz study for relaxation, built from spacious piano and muted trombone phrases over a nearly motionless rhythm foundation.

tempo.feel: Very slow 4/4 with spacious, behind-the-beat swing and occasional held bars that suspend forward motion.

instrumentation.name: piano
instrumentation.role: States the harmonic frame and trades broad phrases with the trombone.
instrumentation.timbre: Soft, resonant, spacious voicings with restrained attack.

instrumentation.name: muted trombone
instrumentation.role: Carries a wide descending melody and answers the piano.
instrumentation.timbre: Veiled, breathy, rounded brass tone with gentle falls and sustained notes.

instrumentation.name: upright bass
instrumentation.role: Provides stable roots and a nearly motionless low-register foundation.
instrumentation.timbre: Warm, woody pizzicato with occasional sustained resonance.

instrumentation.name: brushes
instrumentation.role: Maintains a barely moving pulse and marks phrase transitions.
instrumentation.timbre: Soft circular swishes, sparse cymbal shimmer, no strong backbeat.

structure.direction: Piano alone presents sparse minor, dominant-sus, and ambiguous major sonorities with chromatic descending inner voices.
Muted trombone enters with a broad descending line; bass and brushes join quietly beneath the piano.
Piano and trombone trade spacious phrases, gradually increasing motivic density without increasing volume; keep roots stable while inner voices descend chromatically.
Phrases shorten and soften as piano and trombone converge on an open interval over a restrained bass resonance.
Let the final open sonority decay naturally, softened and unresolved rather than cadential.

production: Intimate acoustic room, warm low-register presence, soft dynamics, moderate stereo width, gentle natural reverberation, clear separation between piano and muted trombone, no dramatic buildup.
assumptions: Target tempo set near 48 BPM to support the specified very slow swing.
The tonic remains deliberately unspecified to preserve harmonic ambiguity.
lyriaPrompt: Late-night noir jazz for relaxation, 150 seconds, very slow 4/4 at about 48 BPM with spacious behind-the-beat swing and occasional held bars. Instrumental only, no vocals. Intimate acoustic quartet: soft resonant piano presents the harmonic frame, muted trombone answers with broad breathy descending phrases, upright bass holds stable roots, and sparse brushes create a nearly motionless pulse. Use minor-centered harmony with chromatic descending inner voices, dominant-sus chords, and ambiguous major sonorities; sustain tension without harshness. [Intro] Piano alone, spacious and shadowed. [Theme] Add bass, brushes, and muted trombone. [Dialogue] Trade broad phrases and gradually increase density without getting louder. [Coda] Converge on a quiet open interval. [Outro] Let it decay into a softened unresolved ending. Warm, restrained, tactile acoustic production with gentle room reverb; avoid bright brass, flashy virtuosity, strong backbeat, abrupt transitions, vocals, and cinematic bombast.
